sections.heading: Interface
items: Workspace headers share the same height, centered labels and separator, including enlarged interface text.
New conversation is inactive when the current chat is already empty; starting a new conversation from existing content preserves the draft and focuses the input.
Pipeline tabs remain on one line. Completed phases use a quiet approval checkmark without repetitive approval subtitles.
Unified readable text, controls and project accents across Welcome, Settings, the editing workspace, cockpit and supporting windows. Interface text can be enlarged in Settings.
Each project retains its format-pack accent across its panels and sheets, while global windows stay neutral and media colors remain unchanged.

sections.heading: Production intelligence
items: Music Video now selects only the production doctrine, camera, story, continuity, and production-sheet guidance relevant to the current phase and intent, within a deterministic context budget.
Shot planning and sanity checks can evaluate visible-character, duration, and reference demands against the selected generation route instead of fixed global limits.

Inherited, defensive, stale, or conflicting model specifications can be researched from Models settings in an isolated Claude web session, reviewed field by field, and saved as reversible local evidence without weakening live provider limits.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Continue uses the explicitly approved target pack after a project upgrade, and preparation failures appear in the Agent panel.
Project pack upgrades now reopen their authorized migrated recovery copy, preserving unsaved work and leaving the saved project untouched until Save.
Storyboard approval now opens the current storyboard in a readable view and checks its current source and gate readiness before approval.
Removing an installed format-pack version keeps confirmation actionable, rechecks project use and reports blocked removals or filesystem errors.
Generated Agent images now open from a legible preview into a bounded viewer with fit and zoom controls.
Spend approval remembers the last confirmed provider and model per media type, changes choices without repeated credential discovery, and shows only relevant provider diagnostics.
Completed paid generations resume their existing Agent runtime without a false connection-loss interruption.
Project saves refresh the package modification date after host writes, preventing false external-change warnings.
Treatment can begin with Agent-proposed variants instead of requiring an uploaded document, and current Higgsfield job_type catalogs remain discoverable and runnable.

sections.heading: Agent
items: Agent conversations now group each request, answer, activity, generated media, and durable workflow receipt into one calm semantic turn with progressively disclosed technical detail.
The Composer Dock now shows either the editor or one required decision, preserves drafts and references across decisions, and keeps large searchable media choices within a bounded surface.
One conversation navigator replaces competing tabs and history controls, while current status, recoverable errors, required actions, and completed provenance each have one visible owner.
The complete Agent surface remains keyboard and VoiceOver accessible, stable under streaming and progress updates, and responsive across compact, standard, and wide panel widths.

sections.heading: Generation and pipeline
items: Format packs can publish format-neutral execution inputs, production routing, source bindings, and exact-byte provenance without moving project truth out of the host.

Model selection and validation now derive duration, resolution, reference, and provider-route limits from versioned capabilities, including the verified Seedance 2.5 480p/720p and 4–30-second contract.
Imported and AI-enhanced shots retain their declared project-local source and deterministic render route through planning, approval, and final provenance checks.

sections.heading: Integrations
items: The built-in MCP server and connected generation providers now negotiate the sessionless MCP 2026-07-28 protocol while retaining compatibility with existing initialize-based clients and servers.
Modern MCP requests validate per-request identity, capability, routing, cache, and custom-header contracts; provider-authored MCP Apps remain outside the Agent transcript and prompt path.

sections.heading: Generation providers
items: fal.ai image choices now come from the authenticated active-model catalog and include the current Nano Banana, Nano Banana 2, Nano Banana Pro, and GPT Image 2 generation and editing endpoints.

Connected Higgsfield models use the provider's complete paged tool catalog, cached and bounded per-model reference discovery, job-set identifier, and validated status/display lifecycle; status-only and synchronous MCP contracts remain runnable when their live schemas support them.
Malformed MCP catalog pages and media-result schemas now fail closed before publication or spend, preserving the last verified model catalog and exposing only outputs the runtime can parse.
Temporary fal.ai catalog failures retain the last verified runnable model set, while rejected credentials fail closed with an actionable Settings state.

Google AI and Runway catalog authentication, malformed responses, incomplete pagination, transient task polling, and uncertain submissions now fail closed without publishing partial models, repeating paid work, or releasing ambiguous spend.
Accepted fal.ai, Runway, and MCP work is cancelled at the provider when local polling or user cancellation stops; failed cancellation remains visible with a possible-charge warning.
MCP spend is recorded only after the provider request is dispatched, and completed work remains queued for its exact originating chat across tab changes.

After approval, image, video, audio, and upscale work moves into a cancellable running state without blocking the composer; completion, failure, or cancellation returns exactly once to the originating chat.

sections.heading: Generation pipeline
items: Production Design lighting anchors pass every staged style reference into a compatible image model and display the completed generated image directly in the agent transcript.
Corrupt, unsupported, oversized, symlinked, or approval-time changed Production Design references now stop generation with the exact staged path instead of being silently omitted.
Approved Production Design reference bytes are copied into an immutable task-local staging area before provider upload, closing the approval-to-render mutation window.

sections.heading: Interface
items: The project-version update dialog now uses native readable body text instead of low-contrast white text.

sections.heading: Generation providers
items: Completed spend and phase approvals now resume the exact originating agent session automatically instead of waiting for another chat message or continuing with stale card state.
A host follow-up that cannot start remains visible and retryable instead of silently returning the agent to Ready.

Higgsfield discovery now accepts the provider's current job-set catalog shape, preserves the selected model identifier during dispatch, and waits for connected catalogs before opening a generation approval.

sections.heading: Generation providers
items: Approved image, video, audio, upscale, and provider-tool requests now start exactly once from the host-owned card and resume the originating chat after submission without holding an MCP request open.

Connected provider catalogs now publish independently as discovery completes, so Higgsfield and other slower services can appear in an already-open spend approval instead of being hidden behind the first provider.
Pending generation approvals no longer keep a closed project in memory.

sections.heading: Generation providers
items: Reference-driven image requests now offer every connected provider and model whose live limits match the assigned media, including Runway and Higgsfield routes alongside fal.ai.

Provider dispatch now preserves each model's declared reference range, maps Higgsfield uploads to the live tool schema, and replaces an unusable saved selection with a runnable option before requesting spend approval.

sections.heading: Generation providers
items: Provider and model discovery now completes before generation tools run, and open spend approvals update when connected capabilities change.
Expired OAuth sessions no longer appear connected or create anonymous provider clients; recoverable outages retain their refresh credentials while rejected sessions request a new sign-in.
Nano Banana image edits preserve the requested aspect ratio, and fal.ai queue jobs use validated lifecycle URLs without repeating submissions whose outcome is unknown.

sections.heading: Generation pipeline
items: Agent video-to-audio generation now routes assigned media and timeline spans through the selected provider instead of stopping after source preparation.
Provider catalog, OAuth, spend-selection, image, video, audio, and upscale paths now expose actionable diagnostics without recording prompts or credentials.

sections.heading: Generation providers
items: Reference-driven MCP generation now maps prompts and media to each provider's live tool schema while preserving every assigned input and its role.
Local references now upload through the selected provider, asynchronous jobs complete without duplicate generation submissions, and only verified generated media is imported.

fal.ai queue jobs now poll and fetch results from the owning application route, retry transient lifecycle failures, and cancel abandoned jobs, restoring image, video, audio, and upscale endpoints that use operation-specific submit paths.

Higgsfield's live image catalog is available without a separate job-status tool, including Nano Banana and GPT Image models exposed by the connected account, while MCP generation supports both direct results and asynchronous jobs.

sections.heading: Agent workflow
items: The composer now presents exactly one dialog, spend decision, or phase approval at a time and refuses competing requests until the open decision is resolved.

sections.heading: Format packs
items: Opening a project with an older pinned format pack now lets you upgrade a Recovery copy to a compatible installed version or continue with the exact pinned version.
Installed pack versions are listed separately, and versions unused by open or registered projects can be removed safely.

sections.heading: Agent integrations
items: Agent settings now imports and manages external MCP servers, keeps complete configurations in the macOS Keychain, requires explicit trust for local commands, and rejects insecure remote connections.

sections.heading: Editor
items: Media import and project commands that were previously unreachable are now available from their native editor and menu locations.
Animation can be cleared from a keyframe context menu with full undo and redo support.

sections.heading: Agent workflow
items: Current agent activity now stays visible beside the composer during long operations, so completed analysis reports cannot hide whether NexGenVideo is still working, waiting, or finished.
Pending direction cards and imported creative references remain represented in the conversation as the workflow advances instead of leaving the transcript anchored on an older Audio Analysis message.
Long suggested answers use compact labels, while their complete values remain intact when submitted.
Claude readiness now appears as soon as chat opens instead of becoming visible only after the first interaction.

sections.heading: Generation providers
items: Spend approval now lets you switch among enabled provider and model combinations that can actually run, without cancelling and restarting the generation.
The selected provider and model stay bound through prompt compilation, pricing, media hosting, and dispatch.

MCP generation now adapts image, video, audio, and upscale arguments to each provider's live tool schema, including nested Higgsfield parameters, while preserving typed workflow values and actionable provider errors.

sections.heading: Projects
items: Saving a project no longer reports a false external-change conflict after NexGenVideo's own coordinated package updates.

sections.heading: Home and editor
items: Home now restores undersized windows to the supported minimum, and the format chooser shows every available format card and description without scrolling.
The composer paperclip now offers both existing reference assets and new file imports without adding a separate row above the prompt.
Structured dialog choices appear as compact selections instead of messages that look user-typed; actual free-text responses remain user messages.
Models settings now shows only models that can run through an enabled provider and updates immediately when provider availability changes.

sections.heading: Agent and workflows
items: Production approvals now remain pending in durable cards without blocking a tool call, timing out, retrying, or inventing a user decline.
Pattern Fit now ranks every valid authored profile immediately, reports library coverage and invalid profiles, and never waits for a fully authored library.
Agent tool schemas now reject unknown fields at both Anthropic and MCP boundaries while preserving explicitly typed dynamic maps.
Agent feedback is recorded honestly in local-only diagnostics; it no longer claims that a team was notified or an external report was sent.

sections.heading: Projects and documentation
items: Media imports now require a saved project and either complete a project-local copy or fail without registering a fragile external-path asset.
Developer documentation now reflects external signed format packs, NexGenVideo-hosted search models, and GitHub Actions as the only build and verification path.

sections.heading: Generation
items: Seedance 2.5 is integrated through fal.ai and recognized across Higgsfield discovery, with automatic or 4–30-second duration, 480p and 720p output, and up to 50 mixed references where supported.
Music Video duration checks now read versioned pack capability data instead of enforcing a hardcoded 15-second Seedance limit.

sections.heading: Compatibility
items: NexGenVideo requires the latest released macOS, currently macOS 26. The macOS 27 Music Understanding adapter remains dormant until that OS ships.
Music Video packs that use the new lyric-alignment and declarative cockpit capabilities now require engine contract 8, so an older host rejects them instead of silently degrading analysis.

sections.heading: Audio analysis
items: The macOS 26 production pipeline now runs the same on-device decoder, stem separation, Whisper lyric alignment, neural beat grid, harmony recognition, and evidence-based structure resolver in the app and private acceptance workflow.

Lyric timing now uses a dedicated known-text alignment capability and falls back from an unusable isolated vocal stem to the original mix, selecting the stronger measured alignment instead of accepting an empty transcript match.
Whisper automatic language selection now continues into transcription instead of stopping after language detection.
Attached lyrics constrain every Whisper decode window while attention-DTW supplies acoustic token timing, and text from windows identified as non-speech cannot become structural evidence.

A host-recorded measurement proof now binds lyric timing to the exact track, lyrics, alignment source, attention-DTW method, anchor counts, and canonical alignment bytes before an interpretation can be written or approved.
Lyrics without section markers now complete after a good known-text alignment instead of triggering redundant weaker transcription passes or a false acceptance failure.
Private exact-file acceptance runs now preserve every available analysis artifact plus exact private failure provenance across runner, structural-gate, and independent-expectation failures.

Canonical song sections now require independently reproducible bar-aligned detector or known-text alignment evidence; ordinary speech recognition can label acoustic boundaries but cannot create timing.
Outro resolution now chooses the first strongest terminal consensus after the final lyric section instead of misclassifying a later instrumental tag as the outro start.
Apple Music Understanding's section, segment, and phrase hierarchy is preserved as a stronger availability-gated strategy for macOS 27.
Out-of-order and non-finite system rhythm samples are normalized deterministically before structural validation.
Optional system rhythm and structure are validated independently before either is selected as canonical evidence.
The Analysis surface now shows exact nested section, segment, and phrase ranges and opens from both its cockpit tab and the Pipeline phase row.
Re-running analysis keeps the last-known measurements visible under runner-reported progress until the replacement artifact is ready.
Xcode 27 builds now compile Metal resources from source and stage consumer-derived binary frameworks through explicit, independently verified runtime boundaries.
Upgrading an existing Music Video project resets Audio Analysis and downstream approvals so the new measured evidence record is established before work continues.

sections.heading: Production planning
items: Reusable production profiles now carry renderability, continuity, rescue-cut, and narrative-beat discipline across compatible format packs.
New generated and AI-enhanced shots store structured production plans while imported footage and existing projects keep their real source truth without invented creative decisions.
Compiled provider prompts and generated media are now bound to the exact project, shot, approved action, camera move, rescue cut, and production plan through final render approval.
Frames and renders with prompts from an older production-plan revision are regenerated instead of being treated as complete.
AI-enhanced renders now require the exact project-local source declared by the Shot List before generation can start.
Still-frame prompts reject camera-motion language, and ensemble member counts now enforce the two-visible-character generation limit.

sections.heading: Stability
items: Agent conversations now follow streaming output through the scroll view's native size-change anchor instead of issuing reentrant scroll commands during layout.
Native Shot List edits now share the pipeline execution lock and crash-recovery marker with agent edits.

sections.heading: Format packs
items: Compatible projects keep opening their exact pinned format-pack version under engine contract 5; genuinely incompatible packs offer an explicit Recovery-copy upgrade instead of loading unsafe code.

sections.heading: Stability
items: Importing or relinking large media now keeps hashing and file copies off the main thread, with visible progress, cancellation, and rollback on failure.

sections.heading: Agent
items: Done now finishes repeatable character and location intake without requiring another reference image.
A started character or location item can be cleared explicitly before finishing the optional intake.
The music-shaping dialog now submits its direction reliably instead of closing without starting generation.

sections.heading: Home
items: The Trash control on a recent project now opens deletion confirmation without opening the project.

sections.heading: Editor
items: The main window now uses more of the available screen height and a taller cap on unusually large desktops.

sections.heading: Home
items: Closing What's New now removes its blocking layer immediately, so Home controls remain clickable without switching away and back.

sections.heading: Stability
items: Prepared character and location cards now advance without briefly exposing the composer, while image copies stay off the main thread and the agent transcript remains responsive.

sections.heading: Format packs
items: Format-pack update notices no longer block Home input, and restarting now completes within a bounded interval, activates the installed version, and returns to an interactive Home window.

sections.heading: Format packs
items: Restarting after a format-pack update no longer leaves the Home window blocked when no project is open.

sections.heading: Format packs
items: Restart NexGenVideo reliably activates an installed format-pack update and reports an invalid restart state instead of doing nothing.

sections.heading: Stability
items: Agent conversations remain responsive while a decision card waits for an answer.

sections.heading: Stability
items: The main-thread watchdog no longer terminates the app at launch.
Swift runtime traps now retain their original stack in macOS crash reports.

sections.heading: Agent
items: Agent transcripts remain responsive when Brief opens after Audio Analysis.
Main-thread stalls now save recent pipeline state and, when available, a process sample under Help → Reveal Diagnostics.

sections.heading: Projects
items: Unsaved timelines, media, chats, and generation state now recover together.
Save, Save As, media import, and song replacement now preserve one complete project state.
Home shows update and restart notices in a dedicated actionable region instead of beside the page title.
Imported media keeps its original filename while content-addressed storage names remain internal.

sections.heading: Agent
items: App controls no longer appear as messages you typed.
Tool failures and approval refusals now stay actionable without exposing internal instructions.
Format-pack analysis errors now keep their actionable instructions instead of collapsing to a generic failure.
Audio analysis stays connected across MCP requests, runs on an isolated worker without starving MCP or media traffic, shows its current stage, and cannot be approved while work is incomplete.
Overlapping pipeline refreshes now settle to one current project state before the workflow continues.
The agent defaults to the app's interface language and changes language only when requested.
Disabled actions now use one unmistakable app-wide visual state instead of retaining active-button contrast.
Agent transcripts remain responsive while pipeline progress, reports, and decision cards update.

sections.heading: Generation
items: The project budget stop now guards every paid generation path before provider dispatch.
Provider pricing, reservations, and verified charges now share one project ledger.

sections.heading: Format packs
items: Downloaded packs are signed, notarized, integrity-checked, and load-tested under quarantine.
Release previews use isolated plugin channels; stable publication happens only after the app release succeeds.
Projects pin their exact format-pack version; updates remain visible and require an explicit, recoverable project upgrade.
Music video production now analyzes the assigned track and optional lyrics before it asks for existing story material.
Prepared character and location intake now numbers each item, requires a complete item before attachment, and provides explicit Skip and Done actions.

sections.heading: Agent
items: Attach project media directly from the composer.
Workflow starters no longer appear as messages you typed.
Existing chat sessions remain compatible with the updated transcript format.

sections.heading: Format packs
items: The active format now has a visible workspace identity and accent.
Music Video uses clearer starter copy and human-readable phase names.

items: New export_project tool - Agent can now export videos for you.
New remove_words tool - Agent can now read your timeline, and remove filler words.

items: Change project settings in the inspector panel - edit fps, resolution, and aspect ratio.
